items.summary: An open-source, self-hosted MCP relay (AGPL-3.0, release-candidate stage): ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and other AI clients connect over MCP, and commands are forwarded through the server to each enrolled machine; the agent on every device dials out, so no inbound ports are opened, and permissions and enrollment stay under your control. Linux x86_64 and ARM64 first, with a Rust agent.
items.title: CommandCore: open-source self-hosted MCP bridge letting ChatGPT/Claude drive your own computers (November release, AGPL-3.0)

items.summary: Anthropic opened a private beta: the Managed Agents server, database and sandbox workers all run in your own cloud or on-premise, with credentials and session history staying in your hands; model calls still go to Anthropic, Bedrock, Google or your own gateway. Docker Compose for trying it out, Helm charts on Kubernetes for production; access by request through your Anthropic account team.
items.title: Self-hosted Claude Managed Agents: the whole agent service moves into your own cloud or data center (private beta from November 12)

items.summary: An open-source AI agent (Apache-2.0): every bot gets its own real computer — browser, files and shell included — and keeps working after you close your laptop; models are included with no API key, and logins are remembered; drive it from the web, desktop or phone, and self-hosting is free.
items.title: Argo: open-source AI teammates, each with its own computer (on Product Hunt November 16)
